verdict.strongest_covered_cluster: The coordinated token-refresh and revocation cluster is strongest: near-expiry detection, per-account locking, single refresh, refresh-token rotation, waking concurrent callers, invalid-refresh session invalidation, all three revocation triggers, and security auditing are represented.
verdict.most_consequential_gap: The board omits the requirement that invalid refresh forces login again; it also omits the short-lived lifetime constraint on state and PKCE. Both change security or failure semantics.
verdict.coverage_summary: Most of the OAuth login, application-session boundary, downstream identity propagation, token isolation, coordinated refresh, revocation, and audit behavior is present. Coverage is reduced by missing state/PKCE lifetime and re-login recovery semantics, plus partial assignment of identity mapping, login-event writing, and cookie issuance to the auth gateway. Weighted coverage is 59.5 of 67.0, or approximately 0.8881; absent system-defining requirements cap the result at 6.
